title: How cuts and wounds heal
examples: What is the first thing that happens when you get a cut?
How long does it take for a wound to heal completely?

explain.say: When you get a cut, your blood starts to flow out. This is the first thing that happens.
Next, tiny bits in your blood called platelets rush to the area. They help to stop the bleeding.
The platelets help form a temporary plug. This plug is part of the blood clot that seals the wound.
Over time, this clot dries and forms a protective covering called a scab. The scab keeps germs out.
Underneath the scab, your body starts making brand new skin cells. These cells grow to cover the wound completely.
Sometimes, when the skin heals, it does not look exactly like before. This difference is what we call a scar.

draw.text: Scar tissue marks the healed area.

faq.q: Why does blood clot when I get a cut?
faq.a: Blood clots because the platelets rush to the site and form a plug. This stops the bleeding so you can stop losing blood.
asks: What is the purpose of blood clotting?
How does my body stop bleeding from a cut?

faq.q: Are scabs always good for healing?
faq.a: Yes, scabs are good because they act as a physical barrier. They keep dirt and germs from getting into the open wound.
asks: Should I always pick at scabs?
What is the job of a scab?

faq.q: How does new skin grow back?
faq.a: New skin cells multiply and move across the wound bed. They fill in the gap left by the injury slowly over time.
asks: What happens after the scab falls off?
Where do the new skin cells come from?

faq.a: Scars are marks left behind when the skin repairs itself. They are usually different in texture or colour from the original skin.

faq.q: Does the healing process take the same time for everyone?
faq.a: No, the time it takes to heal depends on the wound's depth and size. Some wounds heal faster than others.
asks: Is healing speed related to the wound?
What affects how fast I heal?

facts: Platelets are small blood cells that help stop bleeding.
A blood clot forms first, trapping the blood at the wound.
A scab is a protective layer that forms over the clot.
New skin cells multiply underneath the scab to repair the tissue.

quiz.say: When blood first leaks out of a cut, what is the immediate next step in healing?
quiz.show: What happens after blood flows out?

options.show: New skin cells appear right away.
options.say: New skin cells appear right away.

quiz.why: Platelets are the first responders that gather at the site to start the repair process.

wrong.0: Healing is a step-by-step process that takes time and multiple cells.
wrong.2: The scab forms later, after the blood has started to clot.
wrong.3: New skin cells take time to multiply and grow underneath the clot.

quiz.say: What is the main function of the scab during wound healing?

options.show: It keeps germs out of the wound.
options.say: It keeps germs out of the wound.

options.show: It is the new skin itself.
options.say: It is the new skin itself.

options.show: It is the final healed tissue.
options.say: It is the final healed tissue.

options.show: It stops the blood from clotting.
options.say: It stops the blood from clotting.

quiz.why: The scab acts like a natural bandage, preventing infection from outside germs.

wrong.1: The scab is a dried layer, not the living new skin cells underneath.
wrong.2: The final tissue is the new skin; the scab is temporary protection.
wrong.3: The scab forms after the blood has successfully clotted.

quiz.say: If a wound heals, what remains behind that is different from normal skin?
quiz.show: What is the final mark left?
quiz.why: Scar tissue is the body's way of patching up the injury, which is different from normal skin.

wrong.0: Platelets are used up in the clotting process and are not left behind.
wrong.1: While new skin cells are present, the question asks for the mark left behind, which is the scar.
wrong.3: The blood clot dissolves or is absorbed as healing progresses.
